explanation: Reference executed successfully offline (test 1/2): full matchms tutorial pipeline ran from the staged GNPS-NIH-NATURALPRODUCTSLIBRARY.mgf (1267 spectra) through metadata/peak processing, CosineGreedy and ModifiedCosine all-pairs scoring, per-query match lists, and RDKit structure rendering, producing all four declared export artifacts with the staged input verified byte-identical before and after. Environment: matchms 0.30.2 (last release line that still provides the source-imported `ModifiedCosine` class and is compatible with the base image's Python 3.13 + numpy>=2 via the resolved dependency set), plus its resolved dependencies; Debian packages libxrender1/libxext6/libexpat1 added for RDKit's Draw module (rdkit.Chem.Draw hard-linked libs); matplotlib ran headless via MPLBACKEND=Agg, which the controller's execution environment already sets, preserving all plotting calls. pyyaml was added uncovered only when older matchms lines were evaluated for name compatibility — it is a declared matchms 0.30.2 requirement resolved automatically, not a source code change. The earlier matchms 0.21.1 candidate was rejected before any reference dispatch (numpy 2 requirement of Python 3.13 breaks its Scores.scores_by_query at `int(np.where(...)[0])`, and current matchms 0.33.1 removed the `ModifiedCosine` name); no computation slot was consumed by these static checks. Version choice is an environment fact: the tutorial notebook pins no matchms version (its conda instructions date to matchms ~0.1x), so 0.30.2 is the closest compatible release preserving every imported name and API behavior used by the unmodified source.
source_adaptations: analysis.py line 36: `path_data = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.getcwd()), "data")` (a notebook-relative interactive-session path that also carried the tutorial's 'enter your pathname' comment) replaced with the absolute staged input directory `/work/cache/content`, where stage-inputs.sh places the original MGF file. The file name and bytes loaded (`GNPS-NIH-NATURALPRODUCTSLIBRARY.mgf`, sha256 b7d33f02fa35ebebc2c3e8150c57be014a5f4edd556531a7fc8e52913f985f72, 39095019 bytes, 1267 spectra) are unchanged; the source's own json/pickle exports therefore also write into the writable staged-content directory. No algorithm, filter, threshold, parameter, or data-selection change was made.

stage-inputs.sh downloads the input from the GNPS2 mirror https://external.gnps2.org/gnpslibrary/GNPS-NIH-NATURALPRODUCTSLIBRARY.mgf because the canonical https://gnps-external.ucsd.edu/gnpslibrary/... URL timed out repeatedly during setup; the mirror serves the identical bytes (verified sha256), and the recipe verifies the checksum on every fresh staging with retry/resume. This is a retrieval-path-only adaptation recorded in inputs.json provenance.
unresolved_assumptions: Data-file identity beyond checksum: the MGF was obtained from the GNPS2 mirror of the canonical GNPS library URL named in the notebook narrative; bytes match the documented ~39 MB size and the file contains the expected 1267 GNPS-NIH natural-products spectra with SMILES/PEPMASS metadata, but no independent cryptographic publication of the file hash was available for cross-verification.

Version-equivalence caveat: the tutorial was authored against an early matchms release with no pinned version; matchms 0.30.2 was selected because it is the newest release compatible with the required Python 3.13/numpy 2 stack that still provides every name the unmodified source imports (notably `matchms.similarity.ModifiedCosine`). Numerical agreement of the similarity scores with the original notebook's historical (unrecorded) outputs was not verified; the run executed the source's own algorithms and parameters unmodified.

The raw-file metadata cashed 'Found 0 inchikeys in metadata' is faithful to the original dataset (INCHIAUX=N/A fields observed in the staged file); inchikeys are derived downstream by the source's repair/derive filters, as the tutorial narrative describes.

Dependency-asset review covered the controller-flagged catalog candidates across all installed distributions plus content inspection of the matchms data tables; it is not an exhaustive semantic audit of every installed file.
